new_packages.label: כְּלִי אֲנִי — אוֹתִיּוֹת הַתְּפִלָּה
new_packages.label_en: The Vessel Ani — The Letters of Prayer
new_packages.domain_justification: This package is fully independent of any domain in other Torahs. Torah #73 uniquely develops a letter-analysis of the word אֲנִי (I/me) as the name of the divine receiving vessel for abundance (שְׁפָע). The three letters — א (Aleph = tzaddik = every Jew), י (Yud = machshava = thought), נ (Nun = dibur = malkhut = speech) — are each defined through explicit niqra bechina statements and together constitute the vessel formed when a Jew prays with thought connected to speech. This is not a rehash of the malkhut/dibur concept from other Torahs; it is a specific Torah-73 bechina-cluster where aleph/tzaddik/Israel, yud/machshava, and nun/dibur/malkhut are all parallel aspects of the same vessel-formation reality. The cluster has 10 nodes connected by explicit bechina language and forms an independent coherent domain: the ontology of the three-lettered word Ani as a vessel for divine blessing.
bechina_statements_supporting_this_packa: מַלְכוּת נִקְרָא נוּן (יִנּוֹן שְׁמוֹ — לְשׁוֹן מַלְכוּת)
הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה נִקְרָא יוּד (יוּד עַל שֵׁם הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה נֶאֶמְרָה)

new_packages.label: סְתִים וְגַלְיָא — פְּנִימִיּוּת וְחִיצוֹנִיּוּת
new_packages.label_en: Hidden and Revealed — Inner and Outer
new_packages.domain_justification: This package identifies a structural-ontological duality that frames the entire Torah: every reality (God, Torah) has a hidden dimension (stim, penimit) and a revealed dimension (galya, chitzoniut, levush). The bechina statements are: 'mah shenigla lanu HU halevush veha-chitzoniut' and 'mah shenistar mimenu HU hapenimit'. This constitutes an independent bechina domain of 5 concepts (stim, galya, penimit, chitzoniut, levush) all sharing the essential nature of the revealed-hidden ontological structure. It has 3+ concepts with explicit bechina/haya language and does not overlap with Package 1 (which describes the vessel-formation method) or Package 3 (which describes Torah as medium). This is the metaphysical frame, not the method or the medium. Polarity: neutral — this duality exists in the domain of cosmic structure, not in the good/evil axis.
bechina_statements_supporting_this_packa: מַה שֶּׁנִּגְלֶה לָנוּ הוּא הַלְּבוּשׁ וְחִיצוֹנִיּוּת
הַתּוֹרָה סְתִים וְגַלְיָא (opening statement establishing the duality)

new_packages.label: נוּקְבָא — קַבָּלַת תַּעֲנוּג
new_packages.domain_justification: Torah #73 develops a distinct bechina cluster around the concept of divine reception: whoever receives pleasure from another IS called Nukva (niqra nukvah). This applies to God receiving pleasure from Israel's prayer — becoming, as it were, the feminine/receptive pole. The cluster includes: nukva, mekabel taanug, isha (berod isha), and reakh nikoakh (the sweet savor through which this reception occurs). These 4 concepts share the essential nature of the holy receptive/feminine principle — the divine mode of receiving prayer. This is an independent domain from the vessel-formation cluster (Package 1), which describes what Israel does (forming Ani); Package 4 describes what God does (receiving as Nukva). Three of these concepts (nukva, mekabel taanug, isha) have explicit bechina/niqra markers, forming the required 3+ threshold. This cluster has no equivalent in other Torah packages from this dataset and represents a genuinely new conceptual domain worth flagging.
bechina_statements_supporting_this_packa: מִי שֶׁמְּקַבֵּל תַּעֲנוּג מֵאַחֵר, נִקְרָא נוּקְבָא
נַעֲשֶׂה בְּסוֹד אִשָּׁה (God receives → becomes isha)
אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ לַה' — reakh nikoakh IS the mode of divine reception of prayer

observations:
Torah #73 is a special case in the dataset: the current torahData.js contains ZERO bechina edges for reference===73 (all 3 existing edges are eitza type). This means the dataset has never been enriched with the bechina layer for this Torah. The source text, however, contains at least 12 explicit bechina statements using the canonical markers נִקְרָא, הוּא, and מִלְּשׁוֹן, yielding approximately 22 distinct concept-nodes.

Three independent bechina domains each meet the 3+ concept threshold and represent genuinely new packages not reducible to existing packages in other Torahs:

1. The 'Vessel Ani' package (10 nodes) — a unique letter-analysis of the word Ani as a three-component prayer-vessel, where each letter is identified with a human faculty and a divine quality through explicit niqra statements.

2. The 'Hidden/Revealed Ontology' package (5 nodes) — the metaphysical frame of stim-galya / penimit-chitzoniut that opens the Torah and establishes what is being sought.

3. The 'Nukva / Reception' package (4 nodes) — the divine side of the prayer transaction: God receiving pleasure from prayer, becoming Nukva, and thereby inverting hidden/revealed.

The Torah also includes a small Torah/Water/Revelation cluster (3 nodes: torah_73_packages.json Package 3), which serves as the interpretive anchor for the verse 'ki taavor bamayim' and could stand as a 4th new package — but it is more modestly characterized as a supporting bechina cluster merged into an existing neutral package about Torah-as-water (a common bechina across many Torahs), and is therefore represented as a package in torah_73_packages.json rather than as a 'new independent domain' here.

The good/evil mirror structure: Torah #73 is notably one-sided — it is entirely a positive, constructive teaching about building the prayer-vessel. There is no explicit evil counter-package. The Rebbe does not develop an evil Nukva, an anti-tzaddik, or a broken Ani in this Torah. The evil mirror, if it exists, would operate through the ABSENCE of the vessel — when machshava and dibur are not connected, the Ani is not formed and blessing cannot descend. But this is implied in the eitza chain rather than stated through explicit bechina language as a separate evil cluster. No evil package is proposed for Torah #73.
